speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned you have chronic joint pain; to help narrow down the cause, how long have you been experiencing this, and which specific joints are affected?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Osteoarthritis. The patient's age (69), involvement of weight-bearing joints (hips, knees), and the classic mechanical pattern of pain worsening with activity and improving with rest, along with the first metatarsophalangeal joint involvement, are highly characteristic of degenerative joint disease.
